body: The Paravi Duwa Temple(also spelled Parewi Duwa) is a picturesque Buddhist temple located on a small offshore island in Matara, Sri Lanka. The name "Paravi Duwa" translates to "Pigeon Island".
title: Matara Paravi Duwa Temple

body: We had an amazing experience as this temple.We were greeted by the resident monk who personally guided us through the temple. Showed us where to put our flowers (we’d purchased some water lilies at a vendor in front of the temple), gave us some incense to light and guided us through the sights.At the top he showed us how to ring the bell and once downstairs again he made us a rope bracelet for protection which he tied on our wrist whilst chanting. We were even sent on our way with some fresh cake. The temple is currently under renovation so there is some building material around and they are collecting money for the renovation. It’s well worth it to give them some donations for their endeavours & receive such a personalised glimpse into their practices. We thoroughly enjoyed it and can’t thank the monk enough!
title: Well worth a visit!

body: This temple is beautifully situated on an island in the ocean. The old steel suspension bridge collapsed in 2022. A new bridge was opened in 2023. The old one is still rusting in the water. Maybe there is a reason for that (lack of money? memorial?) but it looks a bit messy. Hard work has been done on the new bridge and the temple is also being refurbished. There are several rooms for prayer and sacrifice. Perhaps not the most beautiful, but the location and views are beautiful. The temple is frequented by locals. And yes you have to pay some, but see it as a donation to this temple that is important to many and deserves a chance.
title: This temple deserves a chance

body: It's worth a visit for the observation deck, which offers beautiful views of the ocean. The temple itself is tiny, there is nothing to see inside. The top floor was undergoing renovations. Entrance 500 rupees. There is a monk who can tie a white thread for a tip.

body: Finding this place is very easy, it is clearly visible from the Matara embankment, there is a bus station nearby. The bridge and the temple itself are new (the temple is still under construction), not yet imbued with Buddhist energy, but the complacency is felt. Entrance fee for foreigners is 500 rupees.
title: Energy of complacency

body: the temple located in front of Matara bus station is a must-see destination when visiting Sri Lanka. With an entrance fee of just 500 LKR(only for foreinger), it's an affordable way to experience the country's rich culture and history.Visitors are required to remove their shoes and dress modestly as a sign of respect to the sacred nature of the temple. Once inside, you'll be surrounded by stunning architecture and intricate decorations, all of which contribute to the peaceful and serene atmosphere.One of the highlights of the temple is the view from the top. As you climb the stairs to the upper levels, you'll be rewarded with panoramic vistas of the surrounding area. It's a great way to take in the beauty of Sri Lanka while also getting a sense of the country's spiritual traditions.Overall, the temple in front of Matara bus station is a must-visit destination for anyone interested in Sri Lankan culture and history. With its beautiful architecture, stunning views, and peaceful atmosphere, it's a great way to experience the best of this beautiful country.
title: temple island

body: I've visited here a couple of weeks ago on a Saturday. Rather than a temple, the place felt like more of a hangout place for school children who are visiting extra school tuition classes. Anyway this is a beautiful setting. Located in a small island, accessible via a bridge right next to the Matara bus stand. The bridge is really dangerous btw. You've got to take extreme caution if you are traveling with kids and elderly people. If something goes wrong you'll find yourself in the sea and good luck not to get hit on a rock. The breeze was mind-blowing and you'll really enjoy if you are a lover of nature. There is a place you can safeguard your shoes so no worries about that. Then to reach the main hall where worships takes place you have to climb further up. At the top the view of the see was amazing. You can see some distance from here. Even the glimpse of Dondra lighhouse located at point dondra. I didn't notice any elderly monks here except for a couple of child monks. I am not sure about how crowded this gets on the other days of the week but on that Saturday we went, it was a bit crowded in the evening. Overall if you want to get a break from the insanely hot sun and relax yourself in the middle of Matara town, this is not a bad option. The risky bridge aside though.
title: A place to find some peace in the middle of a hot and busy town

body: The Paravi Duwa Temple in Matara is located off the Beach Road across what is known as Golden Island Pathway which is a short walk across a bridge to reach the Temple at sea. There are so many Temples in very scenic places in Sri Lanka but this is certainly one of the best for scenery and proximity to the great Indian Ocean. It is a small but nevertheless interesting Buddhist Temple where you will find peace and tranquility and have views of the sea and also of the town. The usual Temple dress code is required.

body: The Matara Paravi Duwa Temple is in a wonderful island location of the coast of this busy, bustling town. The Buddhist Temple can be seen from afar as you drive along the coast road near the centre of town. It is accessible via a bridge and it is well worth taking time to explore this unique attraction which has a very special atmosphere surrounded by the waves near to southern most tipoff the islands. From the bus stand, head to the coast road and the 'Golden Island Pathway' is right in front of you, with the Temple in commanding position.

title: Good for a short walk and good views along the coast at Matara
body: Parey Dewa (Parevi Duwa) is the small island a few meters off the shore at Matara (often referred to as Pigeon Island and occasionally Crow Island) and if you arrive at the main bus station in Matara you can reach it by simply heading towards the sea front and looking for the attractive footbridge that leads across to the island. This gives a good view of the beach and is a nice spot to take a photograph. It was built in 2008 to replace the one seriously damaged by the tsunami four years earlier. Once on the other side there is a combination of steps and steep slope up to the small Buddhist Temple that sits atop the island, the full name for which is the Sri Rohana Uposothagara RajamahaViharaya temple. There is no charge for admission but you may be asked to make a donation on leaving and you will be given a receipt. Any amount is acceptable; even 50 rupees so don't let this put you off.Remove any hat and your footwear as you approach the temple and note the channel surrounding it that contains fish. The interior was dimly lit when we visited and didn't contain anything noteworthy apart from the well displayed Buddha at the front. A walk around the exterior - and the aforementioned channel goes all the way round - gives some good coastal views. A fairly elaborate covered area opposite the temple entrance is home to a seated Buddha with a case housing an ornate gold coloured metal plaque.Unless you have a specific interest or purpose in visiting the temple there isn't a great deal there but the views make for a nice walk and offer the best spot to look out across the beach and along the coast in either direction. As you head back you have the option of walking along the sea front to the right or if you walk back towards the bus station you will see the Dutch ramparts a short distance away to your left on the other side of the road. If you are visiting from Mirissa the cost of the bus journey to Matara is 25 rupees each way at the time of writing while you can also pick up one of the many tuk tuks around for which 500 rupees is the sum generally requested.
